html:
The Treaty of Lisbon of 1859 divided the island of Timor between Portugal and the Netherlands. Portugal kept the east and the enclave of Oecusse; the Dutch took the west, along with Portuguese claims on Flores and Solor.

The line followed the old realms loyal to each side and left pockets on the wrong side. Disputes went on until an arbitration at The Hague settled the border in 1914.

That line is now the border between East Timor and the Indonesian province of East Nusa Tenggara. Oecusse, where the Topasses once ruled from Lifau, is still cut off from the rest of the country.
